manifest.title: 1:1 Founder Product Builder Mentorship
manifest.description: 20-session, ~2h/day mentorship pack for a low-tech junior founder to become independently capable of building and operating a real web/app product with AI coding assistance and senior tech-lead guidance.
manifest.author: huygdv

meta.title: 1:1 Founder Product Builder Mentorship
meta.description: Real-product curriculum: frame → build → productionize → transfer ownership.

nodes.title: 1:1 Founder Product Builder Mentorship
nodes.summary: Outcome-driven mentorship for a low-tech junior founder to independently frame, build, ship and operate a real web/app product with AI coding assistance and senior/tech-lead review.

nodes.title: Product Thinking
nodes.summary: Turn a founder idea into a bounded user problem, value proposition, scope and measurable outcome.

nodes.title: Delivery System
nodes.summary: Break product work into small vertical slices with explicit Definition of Done and feedback loops.

nodes.title: AI Coding Operating Model
nodes.summary: Use coding agents as supervised collaborators: context, plan, implement, test, review and verify.

nodes.title: Web/App Mental Model
nodes.summary: Understand browser, frontend, backend, API, database, network, runtime and deployment boundaries.

nodes.title: Backend & API Engineering
nodes.summary: Design API contracts, validation, business rules, auth and integrations.

nodes.title: Data Engineering Foundations
nodes.summary: Model data, migrate safely, query correctly and reason about transactions.

nodes.title: Quality & Debugging
nodes.summary: Verify AI-generated code with tests, debugging, logs and code review.

nodes.title: Product Security
nodes.summary: Handle identity, authorization, secrets, input validation and common web risks.

nodes.title: Production Delivery
nodes.summary: Deploy environments, CI/CD, observability, performance and failure recovery.

nodes.title: Founder Engineering Autonomy
nodes.summary: Own a feature from idea to production, know when to ask for help and continue evolving independently.

nodes.title: Phase 1 · Frame & Operate
nodes.summary: Establish product scope, delivery discipline, AI workflow and system mental model.

nodes.title: Phase 2 · Build the Core
nodes.summary: Build a complete product slice across frontend, backend, data, identity and reliability.

nodes.title: Phase 3 · Make It Production-Ready
nodes.summary: Add testing, debugging, security, deployment, performance and failure handling.

nodes.title: Phase 4 · Transfer Ownership
nodes.summary: Shift from mentor-led pairing to learner-owned delivery and production operations.

nodes.title: Problem → User → Outcome
nodes.summary: Describe the user problem, who has it, desired behavior change and evidence of value before implementation.

nodes.title: MVP Vertical Slicing
nodes.summary: Cut scope by complete user journey and learning value instead of technical layer.

nodes.title: Definition of Done
nodes.summary: Done includes behavior, validation, tests, UX, deployability and acceptance evidence.

nodes.title: Acceptance Criteria
nodes.summary: Observable examples defining expected behavior for human and AI verification.

nodes.title: AI Context Engineering
nodes.summary: Give coding agents the smallest sufficient product, repository, constraints and acceptance context.

nodes.title: AI Task Specification
nodes.summary: Bound goal, constraints, relevant files, expected behavior and verification commands.

nodes.title: Plan Before Code
nodes.summary: Inspect and propose a change plan before modifying a non-trivial codebase.

nodes.title: AI Build → Verify → Review Loop
nodes.summary: Run checks, inspect diff, exercise behavior, review assumptions and iterate after generated code.

nodes.title: Git Mental Model
nodes.summary: Commit, branch, diff, history and rollback as the safety net for AI-assisted development.

nodes.title: Diff-First Review
nodes.summary: Explain why each meaningful change exists before accepting an AI-generated diff.

nodes.title: Repository Navigation
nodes.summary: Locate entry points, routes, components, services, models, config, tests and deploy files before editing.

nodes.title: Request Lifecycle
nodes.summary: Trace user action from browser UI through API, business logic, database and response.

nodes.title: Environment & Configuration
nodes.summary: Separate code from local/staging/production configuration without leaking secrets.

nodes.title: UI Components & State
nodes.summary: Model user events, local/server state, loading/error states and component responsibility.

nodes.title: API Contract
nodes.summary: Define request, response, status, validation and error semantics shared by frontend/backend.

nodes.title: Authentication
nodes.summary: Establish who the user is with an appropriate session/token strategy.

nodes.title: Authorization
nodes.summary: Decide what an authenticated user may do to a specific resource.

nodes.title: Relational Data Model
nodes.summary: Use entities, keys, relationships and constraints to model durable product data.

nodes.title: Schema Migration
nodes.summary: Evolve database schema predictably with reviewable migrations.

nodes.title: Practical Test Pyramid
nodes.summary: Use unit tests for logic, integration tests for boundaries and a few critical end-to-end journeys.

nodes.title: Systematic Debugging Loop
nodes.summary: Reproduce → narrow → inspect evidence → hypothesis → test → fix → verify.

nodes.title: Code Review
nodes.summary: Evaluate correctness, readability, security, maintainability and product behavior.

nodes.title: Web Security Basics
nodes.summary: Reason about XSS, CSRF, injection, insecure resource access, secrets and dependency risks.

nodes.title: Feature Threat Check
nodes.summary: Before shipping, ask what data, identity, permission and abuse paths the feature introduces.

nodes.title: CI/CD
nodes.summary: Automate repeatable checks and deployments so shipping does not depend on memory.

nodes.title: Local → Staging → Production
nodes.summary: Use explicit environments and promotion steps appropriate to product risk.

nodes.title: Observability
nodes.summary: Use logs, metrics, errors and traces to understand production behavior.

nodes.title: Incident Response
nodes.summary: Detect, contain, recover, communicate and learn from production failures.

nodes.title: Lightweight Architecture Decision
nodes.summary: Record context, options, decision and consequences for expensive-to-reverse choices.

nodes.title: Change Risk
nodes.summary: Estimate blast radius, reversibility, data impact and verification effort before change.

nodes.title: End-to-End Feature Ownership
nodes.summary: Learner frames, plans, builds, tests, deploys and reviews a real feature with mentor checkpoints.

nodes.title: Teach-Back
nodes.summary: Explain architecture, trade-offs and failure modes without reading AI output.

nodes.title: When to Escalate
nodes.summary: Escalate security, irreversible data changes, architecture boundaries and high-blast-radius production issues.

nodes.title: Founder Release Playbook
nodes.summary: Repeatable scope → implement → verify → deploy → monitor → rollback checklist.

nodes.title: Product Engineering Operating System
nodes.summary: Maintain roadmap, technical risks, architecture notes, release history and learning goals together.

nodes.title: Student's Real Product
nodes.summary: The single real web/app used throughout mentorship; concepts must connect to a live product decision or feature.

nodes.title: Product Brief
nodes.summary: One-page problem, target user, core outcome, constraints, MVP journey and non-goals.

nodes.title: Delivery Board
nodes.summary: Ordered vertical slices with acceptance criteria and Definition of Done.

nodes.title: Architecture Map
nodes.summary: Current frontend, backend, data, integrations, environments and trust boundaries.

nodes.title: AI Coding Playbook
nodes.summary: Student-specific context, task spec, planning, diff review, testing and escalation workflow.

nodes.title: Production Readiness Checklist
nodes.summary: Security, config, migration, tests, observability, deploy and rollback checks.

nodes.title: Production Release
nodes.summary: Working real product deployed with at least one complete user journey.

nodes.title: Autonomy Demo
nodes.summary: Student independently takes a fresh requirement from framing to production and explains trade-offs.

nodes.title: Default 2-Hour Session Rhythm
nodes.summary: 10m checkpoint · 20m targeted concept/decision · 70m pair build/debug · 15m review/teach-back · 5m next DoD. Mentor intervention decreases by phase.

nodes.title: Program Exit Criteria
nodes.summary: Student can frame, direct AI, inspect diffs, build frontend/backend/data, test/debug, secure, deploy, observe, recover, explain trade-offs and escalate appropriately.

nodes.title: Session 01 · Product Diagnostic & North Star
nodes.summary: Align real product, founder goal, current repo/stack, user pain, constraints and baseline. DoD: Product Brief plus top risks/unknowns.

nodes.title: Session 02 · MVP Slice & Definition of Done
nodes.summary: Cut the smallest valuable end-to-end journey and acceptance examples. DoD: 3–7 ordered slices; first fits 1–3 sessions.

nodes.title: Session 03 · AI Coding Operating Model
nodes.summary: Set context, task spec, plan-before-code, verification and escalation rules. DoD: AI Coding Playbook v1; student explains why code generation ≠ correctness.

nodes.title: Session 04 · Git, Repo Navigation & Safe Changes
nodes.summary: Map repo and practice branch/diff/commit/rollback on a bounded change. DoD: student locates runtime boundaries, reviews diff and recovers a bad AI change.

nodes.title: Session 05 · Web/App Architecture Mental Model
nodes.summary: Trace a real user action browser → frontend → API/server → database → response. DoD: Architecture Map v1.

nodes.title: Session 06 · Frontend Vertical Slice
nodes.summary: Build/improve one real UI slice with loading, error, empty and success states. DoD: path works locally; student explains state/component responsibilities.

nodes.title: Session 07 · Backend & API Contract
nodes.summary: Design/implement backend boundary for same slice. DoD: contract documented by examples and exercised from real frontend.

nodes.title: Session 08 · Data Model & Safe Migration
nodes.summary: Model entities/relations and ship schema migration. DoD: migration runs cleanly; student explains keys, constraints and transaction boundary.

nodes.title: Session 09 · Identity, Permissions & Secrets
nodes.summary: Implement/audit authentication, authorization and config. DoD: positive/negative access cases tested; no secret in client/repo.

nodes.title: Session 10 · Validation, Errors & Retry Safety
nodes.summary: Harden bad input, expected errors and repeated requests. DoD: failure cases actionable; important writes intentionally retry-safe or documented.

nodes.title: Session 11 · Testing AI-Generated Code
nodes.summary: Build a practical test strategy around real risk. DoD: critical logic/boundary automated; student can name intentionally untested areas.

nodes.title: Session 12 · Debugging & Observability
nodes.summary: Practice real/seeded bug with reproduce/evidence/hypothesis. DoD: bug fixed, regression protected and useful logs/error context exist.

nodes.title: Session 13 · Security Review Before Shipping
nodes.summary: Threat-check current feature and fix highest-value risks. DoD: readiness checklist covers identity, permission, input, secrets and dependencies.

nodes.title: Session 14 · CI/CD & Deployment Environments
nodes.summary: Make build/test/deploy repeatable. DoD: student deploys without mentor typing commands and knows rollback/recovery.

nodes.title: Session 15 · Performance & Database Diagnosis
nodes.summary: Measure one meaningful user path and diagnose bottlenecks. DoD: evidence-based optimization or explicit decision not to optimize.

nodes.title: Session 16 · Jobs, Integrations & Failure Recovery
nodes.summary: Harden slow work/third-party calls with timeout/retry/visibility where relevant. DoD: one async/external failure path has explicit recovery.

nodes.title: Session 17 · Independent Feature Ownership
nodes.summary: Student leads a new real feature; mentor only reviews framing, plan and final diff. DoD: production or release-ready with acceptance evidence.

nodes.title: Session 18 · Refactor & Architecture Debt
nodes.summary: Review debt accumulated through AI-assisted build; improve highest-leverage issue without rewrite. DoD: one meaningful refactor/ADR reduces risk.

nodes.title: Session 19 · Production Simulation
nodes.summary: Handle seeded bug/change under time pressure: triage, communicate, fix, verify, monitor. DoD: systematic incident/change loop.

nodes.title: Session 20 · Founder Autonomy & Next 90 Days
nodes.summary: Fresh requirement end-to-end plus teach-back. DoD: autonomy rubric passes; Release Playbook and 90-day roadmap owned by student.

profiles.title: AI-Assisted Product Builder Autonomy Rubric
profiles.description: Measures how independently the learner can turn a product requirement into a safe production change using AI as a supervised engineering tool.

levels.title: Guided Builder
levels.outcome: Can complete bounded product tasks with mentor framing and active pair support.

requirements.outcome: Explain user problem and target outcome.
Use diff/commit/rollback as a safety net.
Trace a request through the product.
Verify rather than blindly accept generated code.

levels.title: Assisted Feature Owner
levels.outcome: Can own a vertical feature with mentor review at framing, plan and release checkpoints.

requirements.outcome: Cut a feature into a deliverable vertical slice.
Give coding agents bounded, verifiable tasks.
Coordinate frontend/backend behavior through a clear contract.
Model product data with keys and constraints.
Debug using evidence and hypotheses.
Recognize common high-impact web risks.

levels.title: Independent Product Builder
levels.outcome: Can take a normal product feature from idea to production using AI, while escalating high-risk decisions appropriately.

requirements.outcome: Define and verify done beyond generated code.
Own framing, build, test, deploy and review.
Choose useful automated coverage by risk.
Threat-check identity, data and abuse paths.
Ship through repeatable checks/deployment.
Verify production behavior after release.
Know when senior review is required.

levels.title: Founder-Operator
levels.outcome: Can continuously evolve and operate the product, make bounded technical trade-offs and use senior help as leverage rather than dependency.

requirements.outcome: Assess blast radius and reversibility before changes.
Document consequential choices and trade-offs.
Handle production failures systematically.
Run a repeatable release and recovery process.
Balance product roadmap, technical risk and learning.
Explain the system and decisions without outsourcing understanding to AI.

inbox.title: Student baseline & current blockers
inbox.note: Record current stack, what the student can do without AI, what they can do with AI, where they get stuck, and the top 3 dependency risks on the mentor.

inbox.title: Real product repository & environment
inbox.note: Add repo URL, deployed URL, stack, local setup notes and current release state. Keep secrets out of the inbox/export.

inbox.title: Weekly autonomy retro
inbox.note: What can the student now do independently? Where did mentor intervention still unblock them? Which AI-coding anti-pattern repeated? What changes next week?

inbox.title: Next high-risk technical decision
inbox.note: Capture the next security, data, architecture or production decision that should receive tech-lead review before implementation.
